correctness.rationale: The specified GP(12,5) graph has 24 vertices, 36 edges, 120 exhaustively enumerated perfect matchings (two independent vertex-order recursions) and 346822 faces including empty. A canonical 36-stage toggle matching pairs 173357 incidences and leaves 22 critical three-cells, 67 four-cells, and 19 five-cells; all 2282760 Hasse incidences were topologically sorted and the matching is acyclic. Exact signed Morse differential matrices 22x67 and 67x19 are recorded in full and independently reconstructed. They have rational ranks 16 and 19 with maximal-rank minors of determinants +1 and -1, respectively; their product is zero. Hence the homology is free of ranks 6 and 32 in degrees 3 and 4. The CW model is 2-connected, 4-cell attachments are classified by their π3 degrees, and unit 5-cell free attaching degrees allow cancellation after absorbing π4(S3)=Z/2 components by a homotopy self-equivalence. Thus the integral homotopy equivalence to six 3-spheres and thirty-two 4-spheres follows. Reverse-order matching gives independent mod-2 ranks 5 and 18, reproducing the Betti numbers. Only the 24-vertex case is claimed.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Nauru GP(12,5) is 24-vertex bipartite cubic of girth six and 36 edges, not a finite planar honeycomb patch H_{2x2x2}, not an open polygonal line tiling, not a two-row rectangular grid or circular ladder (which has 4-cycles), and not a Möbius ladder (which is nonbipartite at order 24). The displayed hypotheses in the primary theorems therefore do not imply the Nauru classification.

value.rationale: The Nauru graph is a canonical 24-vertex edge- and vertex-symmetric cubic bipartite graph, also GP(12,5) and a toroidal hexagonal graph. Matching extendibility is a natural filtration of the ordinary matching complex and is not determined by the previously studied Nauru independence complex. A complete integral homotopy classification with two adjacent nonzero sphere dimensions (ranks six and thirty-two) is an exact structural invariant not implied by published finite-honeycomb or polygonal-line results. It gives a motivated benchmark at a distinguished larger generalized Petersen graph, rather than an arbitrary slice or numerical side condition. No all-parameter theorem, symmetry representation or downstream application is claimed.
